import { CATEGORIES, type Category } from './types.ts';
import type { CatalogEntry } from './catalog-types.ts';

export type { CatalogEntry };

/**
 * The navigation index.
 *
 * Pure data: no generators, no lesson source strings, no imports of the
 * algorithm modules themselves. That is the entire point. The sidebar renders
 * from this, so opening the app costs a few kilobytes instead of dragging 50+
 * generators and 200+ code listings into the initial bundle. The selected
 * algorithm's module is then fetched with a dynamic `import()`.
 *
 * GENERATED by `npm run gen:catalog` (tools/genCatalog.ts) from the modules' own
 * metadata, because a hand-maintained duplicate of six fields per algorithm is a
 * duplicate that will drift. `contract.test.ts` asserts the two agree, so a
 * forgotten regeneration is a failing test rather than a stale sidebar.
 *
 * The one thing that is *not* generated from the modules is the search
 * vocabulary — `tags` and `aka`. Those are the words a student would actually
 * type ("divide and conquer", "nlogn", "tortoise and hare"), and no amount of
 * reading a module tells you them. They live in `EXTRA` in the generator.
 *
 * Layout of an entry: category order first (the curriculum order, not
 * alphabetical — a student should meet bubble sort before quicksort), then by
 * title within the category.
 */

export const CATALOG: CatalogEntry[] = [
